title: A subject-centred, bounded graph of the pack: search anything, expand its neighbourhood, keep the evidence basis on every edge
problem: A reader has no way to see how the things they care about — a recorded name, a place, a group, a data set — connect, without asking one question at a time. The consumer must not infer identity, group membership or relationships (the id-verification boundary from IDL-REQ-0002/TR-VIS-0003), and pulling raw rows to assemble edges in the browser is the wrong shape at 42k records. What is missing is a bounded search across every node kind and a bounded per-node neighbourhood expansion, so the UI can model the way people think rather than the way the pipeline runs. AMENDED 2026-07-28: the original request framed the primary view as a sources → measurements → entities pipeline; that framing is replaced by this subject-centred one and the fixtures have been rewritten accordingly.
evidence: Everything the graph needs already exists producer-side in aggregate form: audit.source_versions, the estimate target catalogue (source → quantities with count columns), site-orientation denominators, the bounded entity catalogue with per-entity record counts (subject_resolver), and declared entity↔entity pairs (interaction-pairs, 5,622 named frugivory pairs).

The consumer's data explorer already renders source → quantity lists from /v1/estimate/targets; it cannot show which entities those quantities attach to, or how entities relate, because no endpoint aggregates that.

The UX (a full-page 'Atlas' under Data) is built and shipping against the fixture in dss/contracts/fixtures/graph/ — the fixture is the acceptance shape; a labelled sample-data fallback renders until this endpoint exists.

AMENDED 2026-07-28: fixtures rewritten to the subject-centred shape — overview.json (starting points + kind totals), search.json (all-kind alias search incl. the ambiguous 'north'), node-ent-a/ent-c/ent-d/ent-n/grp-one/plc-north/src-alpha.json (relations with basis, provenance, actions, omitted counts). The Atlas UI implements the merge/expand/prominence/budget behaviour against them.
requested_outcome: GET /v1/graph — starting points, not a pipeline: node_kinds (kind, human label, total count) and a small set of suggested starting nodes across kinds (top by records). The consumer renders these as entry chips on an otherwise search-first canvas.

GET /v1/graph?q=<text> — search across EVERY producer-declared node kind and its aliases (subjects, groups, places, sources, measurements). Returns matching nodes (stable id, kind, label, records, aliases); ambiguous terms simply return multiple kinds and the person chooses. Empty result is an empty list, not an error.

GET /v1/graph/node/{id} — the bounded expansion primitive. Returns the node, its relations grouped by a machine relation key with a human label, a per-relation `basis` field distinguishing explicitly recorded relationships ('recorded': declared interactions, group membership, recorded-in-source, recorded-at-place) from derived ones ('derived': shared source, shared location), each neighbor with its edge count, per-relation producer caps with an `omitted` count, a `provenance` list of plain statements, and idli-result/1-shaped `actions`. The consumer calls this repeatedly and MERGES responses by stable id — ids must be stable across calls.

The consumer keeps its own total budgets (nodes/edges on canvas), decays visual prominence with hop distance from the searched node (three hops maximum before re-anchoring), draws recorded edges solid and derived edges dashed-and-lighter (never colour alone), and shows every omitted count. Clicking a node opens details/provenance/actions — an action fills the composer; nothing is auto-sent.
All labels are the pack's own human words — the same screen serves the ecology and livelihoods packs unchanged.
Counts are honest aggregates of admitted records (same audit basis as site-orientation denominators).
Cheap to serve: precomputable at pack index time; pack_digest for cache identity.
acceptance: Searching a term that is both a place and a recorded name returns both, each labelled with its kind; choosing one anchors it dominant on the canvas with its first bounded neighbourhood.
Expanding neighbors three hops from the anchor accretes into one merged graph — prior nodes never move or vanish — and a fourth hop requires re-anchoring.
Every edge carries relation, human label, count and basis; a derived shared-source edge is visibly lighter/dashed next to a recorded interaction edge.
Per-relation omitted counts and consumer budget omissions are visible, never silent.
A group node lists its source-declared members; membership never comes from the consumer.
Node detail shows provenance statements and capability-mapped actions; invoking an action fills the composer without sending.

The fixtures in dss/contracts/fixtures/graph/ (sector-neutral: a subject, a place, a group, a source, five relation types, three progressive hops, an ambiguous search, capped/omitted neighbours) all render live with no consumer change.
notes: The graph is an index, not an analysis engine: clicking a node in the Atlas seeds the mapped question through the conversation, so insight still flows through audited turns. The consumer renders exactly the nodes/edges/labels supplied and never invents membership — same boundary as subject resolution.
